query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Systematically varying the percentage of one or more constituent elements in the HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy will lead to measurable changes in its mechanical properties due to modified solid solution strengthening and microstructural evolution.
generation.material_initial_state: HfNbTaTiZr HEA synthesized in an equiatomic or near-equiatomic state
generation.intervention: Altering the relative percentages of the elemental powders prior to consolidation via powder metallurgy methods
generation.conditions: Using controlled powder metallurgy synthesis (e.g., blending elemental powders followed by spark plasma sintering under inert atmosphere) while keeping sintering parameters, temperature, and pressure constant across samples
generation.structural_mediator: Changes in grain size, phase uniformity, and possible secondary phase formation induced by the compositional shifts
generation.mechanism: Variations in elemental composition are expected to alter the alloy’s solid solution strengthening and phase stability. This can modify dislocation mobility and promote grain refinement or phase segregation, which in turn affects hardness and strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: Samples with increased levels of strengthening elements may show higher hardness and yield strength relative to the baseline equiatomic alloy, although the relationship may be non-linear and bounded to the single-phase stability region.
generation.baseline: The equiatomic (or near-equiatomic) HfNbTaTiZr HEA produced by powder metallurgy and spark plasma sintering, exhibiting a known microstructure and set of mechanical properties
generation.boundary: The observed effects are expected to hold as long as the compositional variations preserve a single-phase solid solution; excessive deviation may lead to phase separation or the formation of detrimental secondary phases.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude and linearity of the mechanical property changes with composition variations remain uncertain without further detailed experimental mapping.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of HfNbTaTiZr HEA samples with one element varied systematically (e.g., increasing Hf from 20% up to 40% while proportionally reducing another element) using the same powder metallurgy process and spark plasma sintering conditions. Characterize the resultant microstructure with SEM/TEM and measure mechanical properties (hardness, compressive/tensile strength) for each composition.
measurements: Grain size and phase distribution via SEM/TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the systematic compositional variation does not lead to any statistically significant change in microstructural features or mechanical properties compared to the equiatomic baseline, the hypothesis that individual percentages of constituent elements affect the mechanical properties is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract High entropy alloys (HEA) have been one of the most attractive groups of materials for researchers in the last several years. Since HEAs are potential candidates for many (e.g., refractory, cryogenic, medical) applications, their properties are studied intensively. The most frequent method of HEA synthesis is arc or induction melting. Powder metallurgy is a perspective technique of alloy synthesis and therefore in this work the possibilities of synthesis of HfNbTaTiZr HEA from powders were studied. Blended elemental powders were sintered, hot isostatically pressed, and subsequently swaged using a special technique of swaging where the sample is enveloped by a titanium alloy. This method does not result in a full density alloy due to cracking during swaging. Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed powders resulted in a fully dense but brittle specimen. The most promising result was obtained by SPS treatment of gas atomized powder with low oxygen content. The microstructure of HfNbTaTiZr specimen prepared this way can be refined by high pressure torsion deformation resulting in a high hardness of 410 HV10 and very fine microstructure with grain size well below 5
